# 1474 — Boundary Quartic Sewing Is Generated by Labelled Image-Line Tensor Products

## Status

First mixed boundary-interaction sewing test following Entries 1468, 1470,
and 1472. The source boundary operator is the dimension-four \(\phi^4\)
operator listed in Collins--Holman, arXiv:hep-th/0507081v1, Eq. (6.8).

## Boundary-to-bulk line

For the source propagator and a physical endpoint \(t>t_0\), restriction of
the second endpoint to the initial hypersurface gives

\[
\boxed{
G_k(t,t_0)
=
\frac{i}{2k}
\left(1+e^{\widetilde\alpha_k}\right)
b_k(t),
\qquad
b_k(t)=e^{-ik(t-t_0)}.
}
\]

The vacuum and image contributions therefore become proportional after
boundary restriction. They do not define two independent outgoing states.
The boundary-to-bulk propagator is one labelled coefficient line per edge.

## Quartic boundary vertex

For four labelled momenta \(k_1,\ldots,k_4\), the tree contribution from one
boundary \(\phi^4\) insertion is proportional to

\[
\delta^3\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^4\mathbf k_i\right)
\prod_{i=1}^4
\left[
\frac{i}{2k_i}
\left(1+e^{\widetilde\alpha_{k_i}}\right)b_{k_i}(t_i)
\right].
\]

Thus its coefficient object is generated by

\[
\boxed{
\bigotimes_{i=1}^4\mathcal L_{\Sigma,k_i}.
}
\]

The four edge occurrences must remain labelled, but no additional nesting,
contact, or propagation primitive is needed. Expanding each factor into
vacuum plus image produces a Boolean occurrence expansion; restriction maps
all terms for a fixed edge to the same one-dimensional line.

## Mixed bulk sewing

Connecting one labelled boundary leg to a bulk vertex inserts the same mode
\(b_k(t)\) into the bulk time integral. Consequently boundary multiplication
and bulk sewing preserve the tensor category generated by the labelled
lines \(\mathcal L_{\Sigma,k}\). Normal derivatives multiply a line by its
boundary jet and remain inside the boundary-local coefficient algebra derived
in Entry 1472.

## Cut comparison

Bulk spectral Cut annihilates an image contribution on any selected internal
occurrence, while boundary restriction retains its coefficient. For a
quartic boundary vertex, the supported kernel is therefore generated by the
tensor ideal containing at least one labelled image factor. This ideal is
intrinsic to the boundary coefficient algebra:

\[
\boxed{
\ker(\operatorname{Cut}_{\rm bulk})\big|_\Sigma
=
\left\langle
\text{labelled tensors with an image-line factor}
\right\rangle.
}
\]

## Narrow conclusion

The first interacting boundary contact closes under

\[
\boxed{
\text{existing background-boundary incidence}
+
\text{labelled tensor products of boundary coefficient lines}.
}
\]

No new carrier stratum is produced. The additional cosmological information
is coefficient-theoretic and support-sensitive.

## Next falsifier

Test a boundary loop or a boundary-to-bulk-to-boundary return path. Unlike the
tree quartic, it integrates products of boundary lines over a loop momentum
and can generate new period or renormalization structure. Freeze the source
boundary operator grading and ask whether every singularity remains on the
declared boundary/soft/Cayley--Menger support. A new integrated period is
allowed as coefficient complexity; only an undeclared incidence support
would falsify H2 at carrier level.
